title: The Arkis instance is bounded by off-chain parameters that no rate limit can enforce
content:
The Arkis instance places two parameters where no other instance has any: under `Off-chain Operational Parameters` it records "The Maximum Exposure for this Instance is $50 million" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.10.1.2.5.1) and "The Instance Capital Ratio Requirement for this Instance is 50%" (.10.1.2.5.2). Its on-chain limits are ordinary: inflow `maxAmount` 5,000,000 USDC with a 5,000,000 per day slope, outflow Unlimited (.10.1.2.4.1/.2).

These are different in kind from everything else in the registry. Every rate limit is a *flow* control that the controller enforces at call time. Maximum Exposure is a **stock** control — a ceiling on the position that may be outstanding at any moment — and the rate-limit machinery has no concept of accumulated balance. A capital ratio requirement is a credit condition on the counterparty, which no Spark contract can observe at all.

The arithmetic makes the gap concrete. A 5,000,000 per day inflow slope reaches $50 million in ten days of continuous drawing, and nothing in the `rateLimited` modifier notices when the eleventh day would breach the documented cap. The constraint is real as governance and invisible as code.

Filing them under `Off-chain Operational Parameters` is therefore an accurate label rather than a filing convenience: it marks exactly which commitments depend on someone watching. It also shows the limits of the whitelist-by-rate-limit design — for a venue whose risk is credit rather than execution, the parameter that matters most is the one the contracts cannot hold.
description: A $50 million Maximum Exposure and a 50% Instance Capital Ratio Requirement sit under Off-chain Operational Parameters, making them process commitments rather than contract-level constraints.
